Here are some schema-themed jokes:

- Why did the database break up with its schema? It needed more space; the schema said, “You can’t just change my type!”
- A schema walks into a bar. Bartender: “We don’t serve your type.” Schema: “Relax, I’m just here to define the fields.”
- I don’t always validate JSON, but when I do, I do it strictly and judge your commas.
- I added schema markup to my dating profile—still no rich results, just poor impressions.
- Went to schema therapy. Turns out my core belief was VARCHAR(20) and I have commitment issues with NOT NULL.
- Our relationship has constraints. I’m foreign-key dependent; you’re primary-key independent.
- I tried mapping my feelings to a schema—turns out they’re unstructured data with eventual consistency.
- My love life is NoSQL: no schema, lots of flexibility, zero joins.
- Told my schema we’re migrating. It said, “ALTER my ego gently.”
- I normalized my life to 3NF—no redundancy, no friends, perfect isolation.
- My calendar must allow NULLs, because it’s always empty.
- I added indexes to my jokes—still no quick laughs; must be a cardinality issue.
- You’re my primary key—unique, not null, and everyone references you.
- I trust CSVs without a schema. I like to live on the edge of the delimiter.
- Tried to model my social graph; turns out I’m a tree. No cycles, no parties.
